words.gloss_range: resumptive coordination opening the third branch of the sorting sequence

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: fused conjunction and branch particle that reopen the sorting frame

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) resumes rather than merely adds. It binds this ayah back to the branch pattern already opened at 56:88 and 56:90, so the listener hears the third classified case arriving inside the same judgment sequence. Because it is written onto the following branch particle as {{ar:وَأَمَّآ}} ({{tr:wa-ammā}}), the turn from the completed peace verdict in 56:91 into the new case feels immediate, continuous, and sharply reoriented.

topics.headline: resumptive connector opens the third case
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this ayah is the third coordinated case in the closing classification, not an isolated afterthought.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the word as a conjunction, and the attachment cross-reference licenses the repeated branch frame anchored at 56:88.

topics.headline: written fusion makes the turn immediate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the branch turning directly out of the previous verdict while remaining inside the same sorting architecture.
topics.reason: The conjunction is proclitic to the following branch particle, so the graphic and syntactic transition both support an immediate resumption.

words.gloss_range: topic-detail branch particle that opens a case and delays its answer

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: inner conditional particle that thickens the third branch

words.prose: {{ar:أَمَّآ}} ({{tr:ammā}}) places the third case before the listener as a branch heading, but it does not let the branch finish inside 56:92. Its answer is pushed forward to 56:93-94, so the ayah becomes a suspended protasis rather than a complete verdict. As the third occurrence in the 56:88, 56:90, and 56:92 sequence, the particle completes the closing triad while making this final branch heavier by standing beside the inner condition {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}). The written long ā also lets the branch marker linger in recitation, matching its job of holding the case open before the delayed answer.

topics.headline: branch particle withholds the answer
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah deliberately opens a case whose consequence must be heard in 56:93-94.
topics.reason: Attachment support explicitly marks the condition in 56:92 and the following result in 56:93, matching the CRITICAL claim that the answer is delayed across the ayah boundary.

topics.headline: third branch completes the sorting frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same branch marker organizes the final outcomes into an ordered three-case classification.
topics.reason: The local particle is tagged as a topic-detail conditional particle, and attachment evidence treats it as the third formulaic branch marker anchored at 56:88.

topics.headline: outer branch meets inner condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this final branch is staged with extra syntactic delay, moving from resolved peace back into suspense.
topics.reason: The branch particle is immediately followed by a separate conditional particle, and the visible clause is licensed as a condition awaiting the next-ayah consequence.

words.gloss_range: conditional particle marking the class membership as a condition under consideration

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: copular verb that forms the core of the protasis

words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) makes the classification conditional before the class is named. The third branch is not phrased as an automatic temporal scene, or as an idhā-style expected occurrence; it is framed as a condition being tested, with {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) and the class phrase forming the protasis. Nested inside {{ar:أَمَّآ}} ({{tr:ammā}}), this particle thickens the final branch: branch heading, condition, class label, and only then the consequence in 56:93.

topics.headline: condition rather than expected occurrence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the condemned classification is grammatically conditional rather than presented as an automatic event.
topics.reason: QAC tags the word as a conditional particle, and attachment support says the classification should remain conditional and wait for its consequence.

topics.headline: inner condition thickens the third branch
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final case has an added inner condition inside the outer branch frame.
topics.reason: The local syntax licenses {{ar:أَمَّآ إِنْ}} ({{tr:ammā in}}) as the front of the visible condition, so the row's claim of stacked conditionality is locally supported.

words.gloss_range: copular condition assigning the implied person to a class; perfect in form but conditional in function
words.root_gloss_range: broad being, occurrence, position, and related branches; local grammar selects copular status assignment with membership through {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}})

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: conditional particle governing the local protasis
partitive predicate opening the class phrase

words.prose: {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}) is perfect in form, but under {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) it serves the conditional protasis, not simple past narration. Its incomplete copular frame pushes forward to {{ar:مِنَ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ}} ({{tr:mina l-mukadhdhibīna}}), where the implied masculine singular person is placed among a defined group. The broad {{ar:ك و ن}} ({{tr:k-w-n}}) field can range from being to position and even the creative command, but here that force narrows into status assignment: the person is not acting through this verb, and no one is being brought into existence; the grammar classifies him. The same verb-frame returns across the nearby final branches at 56:88, 56:90, and 56:92, and here it holds the deniers-and-astray class as a condition awaiting the punishment answer in 56:93-94.

topics.headline: perfect form serves the condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the perfect verb gives the condition a completed contour without turning the line into mere past narration.
topics.reason: QAC gives the verb as perfect, while the immediately preceding conditional particle and translation support require it to function inside the condition.

topics.headline: copular frame assigns class membership
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb does not narrate a fresh action but places the implied person among the deniers-and-astray class.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks {{ar:مِنَ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ}} ({{tr:mina l-mukadhdhibīna l-ḍāllīna}}) as the visible predicate complement of the copular verb.

topics.headline: the subject is carried but not named
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from the direct address of 56:91 to a third-person classification whose subject remains morphologically present but unnamed.
topics.reason: The verb carries 3ms agreement, but attachment evidence warns that no explicit same-surah nominal antecedent is grammatically forced.

topics.headline: being becomes status placement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the broad being-root gives the classification a sense of placement while local grammar blocks creative or causative force.
topics.reason: V4 preserves broad {{ar:ك و ن}} ({{tr:k-w-n}}) branches including being, occurrence, and position, but the local Form I copular frame with {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) selects classification rather than creation, causation, or transformation.

topics.headline: the verb returns in sorting scenes
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same copular frame participates in repeated sorting language, while the local ayah still waits for its punishment answer.
topics.reason: The nearby branches at 56:88 and 56:90 share the verbal frame, and cited formula examples include 26:10 and 28:8; this supports a sorting-template payoff without making distant examples control the local parse.

words.gloss_range: partitive membership preposition governing the following definite plural class
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) chooses membership, not spatial origin. It makes the implied person one from among the definite plural class before that class is fully pronounced. After the direct address of 56:91, this preposition helps withdraw the scene from intimacy into group sorting: the person is placed inside {{ar:ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ}} ({{tr:al-mukadhdhibīna al-ḍāllīna}}).

topics.headline: membership rather than source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition sorts the implied person into a class before the class label is complete.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence shows the preposition governing the definite plural participle as the predicate complement of {{ar:كَانَ}} ({{tr:kāna}}), which selects partitive class membership.

topics.headline: direct address gives way to group sorting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the boundary movement from the directly addressed recipient in 56:91 to a plural classification in 56:92.
topics.reason: The preposition introduces a governed plural class phrase, while the previous ayah's address is no longer the local speech form.

words.gloss_range: definite Form II active participial class: those who actively declare truth false
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes falsehood, lying, denial, and other idioms; local Form II active participle selects declaring or treating truth as false

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: partitive preposition governing the class phrase

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ}} ({{tr:al-mukadhdhibīna}}) is the first named class under {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}), and the following {{ar:ٱلضَّآلِّينَ}} ({{tr:al-ḍāllīna}}) attaches to it rather than starting a second independent group. Its Form II active participle makes the label stronger than simple lying: these are agents characterized by declaring truth false and carrying denial as identity. That identity gathers force from the same-surah thread where denial is an action in 56:82 and the paired label appears in reversed order in 56:51; here the action and earlier address settle into a final class name. Wider recurrence at 7:36, 10:39, and 26:6 supports the category background, while the local proof remains the 56:51 and 56:82 thread. The doubled middle radical gives the falsification label audible pressure, and the shared long -īna cadence with {{ar:ٱلضَّآلِّينَ}} ({{tr:al-ḍāllīna}}) makes the two labels sound like one paired class. Against the peace of 56:91, the word opens the obverse branch.

topics.headline: first participle heads one class phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first participle supplies the governed class head, with the next participle attached to it.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks the word as governed by {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) and the following participle as agreeing with and attaching to it.

topics.headline: Form II participle names active falsifiers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the label means active denial of presented truth, not merely ordinary false speech.
topics.reason: QAC gives a Form II active participle, and V4 preserves the branch of attributing falsehood or denial; the local form selects that branch over unrelated idioms.

topics.headline: denial becomes a people-label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that denial is packaged as a definite plural class of persons rather than as an abstract action.
topics.reason: The word is a definite masculine plural active participle, so the morphology supports an identifiable group of agents rather than a verbal noun.

topics.headline: earlier denial returns as final identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that denial shown as action in 56:82 and as a paired address in 56:51 becomes a final classification in 56:92.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence explicitly links the phrase to the class from 56:51, and the CRITICAL rows supply the same-surah denial action at 56:82.

topics.headline: wider recurrence supports category language
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the class label is not new in tone; it stands in a wider denial-category field while the local proof rests on 56:51 and 56:82.
topics.reason: The cited wider references include 7:36, 10:39, and 26:6, but the local argument is narrowed to the licensed same-surah recurrence at 56:51 and 56:82.

topics.headline: sound and boundary sharpen the label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices both the audible pressure of the doubled middle consonant and the semantic contrast with the prior peace verdict.
topics.reason: The Form II participle accounts for the doubled middle radical, and the paired participles share the same plural cadence at the boundary after 56:91.

topics.headline: denial is the entry point
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that active denial comes first and lostness arrives as the explanatory or qualifying tail.
topics.reason: The local sequence places {{ar:ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ}} ({{tr:al-mukadhdhibīna}}) before {{ar:ٱلضَّآلِّينَ}} ({{tr:al-ḍāllīna}}), and attachment evidence treats them as one governed phrase.

words.gloss_range: definite Form I active participial label for those astray, attached to the deniers as qualifier or apposition
words.root_gloss_range: root range includes going astray from guidance, being lost, disappearing, failing to locate, forgetting, and stray-animal imagery; local Form I participle selects state of lostness or deviation, not explicit causation
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلضَّآلِّينَ}} ({{tr:al-ḍāllīna}}) closes the ayah as the attached second label of the same governed phrase. Its agreement and matching definite plural shape with {{ar:ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ}} ({{tr:al-mukadhdhibīna}}) let it clarify, substitute for, or adjectivally qualify the deniers, but not create a separate coordinated class. Lexically, the Form I participle keeps the focus on people in lostness and deviation; the broader {{ar:ض ل ل}} ({{tr:ḍ-l-l}}) field contributes path-loss and disappearance pressure while the local form stops short of saying they are explicitly causing others to stray. The same form recalls the excluded path-category at 1:7, and the same denial-lostness pair returns from 56:51 in reversed sequence, now as the terminal classification phrase. Its assimilated article and emphatic onset give the final label a heavy joined sound. In final position, the word leaves lostness ringing after the peace of 56:91 and before the answer in 56:93.

topics.headline: matching form locks the apposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second participle is grammatically attached to the deniers, not introduced as a fresh group.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence marks agreement in definiteness, plurality, gender, and genitive case, supporting modifier, apposition, or clarifying attachment rather than coordination.

topics.headline: parallel plural shape binds the pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the matching definite plural shape makes denial and lostness one compound identity.
topics.reason: Both words are definite masculine plural active participles in the same governed phrase, so the pair reads as a compound class identity.

topics.headline: path-loss colors moral deviation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that moral deviation is colored by concrete path-loss and disappearance imagery, while causative misguiding remains only background.
topics.reason: V4 preserves branches for going astray, being hidden, and being lost, but QAC gives the local word as a Form I active participle, so causative leading-astray cannot govern the local sense.

topics.headline: participle makes lostness personal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word names persons in a state of deviation, not an abstract condition and not explicit misguiders.
topics.reason: The local morphology is a Form I active participle, which personalizes the state and blocks treating the word as a verbal noun or causative Form IV label.

topics.headline: the final label echoes known path-categories
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same form recalls the excluded path-category of 1:7 and the reversed same-surah pair at 56:51.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows cite the exact-form comparison with 1:7 and the same-surah paired participles at 56:51; attachment evidence licenses the 56:51 discourse reference.

topics.headline: cross-surah field is apparatus
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a broader formula field around the participial label, but the local payoff remains the final branch phrase at 56:92.
topics.reason: The wider comparison with 1:7 is useful, and 56:51 is locally licensed; claims about a full tripartite humanity scheme are kept as apparatus rather than made to govern the local parse.

topics.headline: lostness seals the suspended ayah
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends on lostness, reversing the prior peace and leaving the punishment answer suspended until 56:93.
topics.reason: The word is final in 56:92, and attachment support says the consequence appears in 56:93, so the boundary and delayed-answer claims are locally supported.

topics.headline: heavy onset marks the closing label
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the fused article and emphatic onset give the final lostness label audible weight at the boundary.
topics.reason: The local surface begins with the assimilated definite article before the emphatic initial consonant, supporting the phonetic-row payoff without changing the grammar.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The conditional كَانَ مِنَ construction places the subject among the active مُكَذِّبِينَ and the directionally marked ضَّآلِّينَ.
baseline_models.mechanism: The clause combines an instantiated condition, an active attribution of falsehood, and departure from an aim. It therefore presents a class defined by both stance and orientation, without deciding whether denial causes straying or straying enables denial.

activation_trace.role: Occurrence and presence in time make the classification a realized condition rather than a free-floating description.
Attributing a thing or speaker to falsehood supplies the class's active oppositional stance.
Deviation from guidance and aim supplies the class's failed orientation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: مُكَذِّبِينَ names active false-attribution, while the focus root of ضَّآلِّينَ also carries disappearance and loss.
baseline_models.mechanism: The pairing can describe a damaged relation to what is denied: the subject does not merely take a wrong road but treats something as false while it has gone missing from view. This preserves a perceptual reading alongside the directional one.

activation_trace.role: Active assignment to falsehood supplies the rejecting relation to the denied referent.
Disappearance and hiddenness recast straying as loss of perceptual access.
Loss of a thing sharpens the model from general error to a relation in which the referent cannot be found.

changed_reading.after: The deniers are also those for whom what they reject has become hidden, lost, or unfindable.

context_deltas.mechanism: The sequence moves from fixed stellar locations and a prominent celestial marker to recited, written, and delivered discourse. Against that field, ضَّآلِّينَ can mark failed orientation in the presence of supplied coordinates, while مُكَذِّبِينَ names rejection of the guide that could orient them.

activation_trace.role: Falling and becoming fixed supply stable locations that can function as coordinates.
A prominent marker supplies the visible sign by which orientation is possible.
Reading and recitation turn the orienting sign into articulated discourse.
Ordered letters and a written object give the discourse durable, inspectable form.
Sending down and conveying supply the movement by which the guide reaches its hearers.
Deviation from aim anchors the contextual signs back to the focus label.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fixed locations, a prominent marker, and delivered writing; the reader supplies the arrow that these operate as coordinates and guide. A live alternative is that they function only as evidence of authority, not as navigation.

changed_reading.after: ضَّآلِّينَ can indicate failure to orient despite fixed signs and an articulated guide, with denial acting as rejection of those coordinates.

context_deltas.mechanism: The discourse is first met with smoothing accommodation and then provision is actively made into denial. The later nominal class مُكَذِّبِينَ therefore gathers up a practiced conversion of what is received into a false-attributing response, not merely a private opinion.

activation_trace.role: Soft accommodation and evasive conciliation supply a preliminary mode of handling the discourse without square acceptance.

The same false-attributing root anchors the earlier practice in the focus's agentive class label.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies smoothing, making, allotted provision, and denial; the reader supplies the conversion arrow from gift to rejecting response. The live alternative is that denial constitutes their treatment of provision without implying a literal exchange.

strongest_changes: The repeated ك ذ ب in 56:82 turns denial from opinion into a configured response to provision.
The deathbed challenge in 56:83-87 recasts the label as a claim exposed under an irreversible practical test.
The parallel conditionals in 56:88-94 make كَانَ مِنَ a formal classification whose third outcome is an inverted reception.
The located signs and delivered writing of 56:75-80 sharpen ضَّآلِّينَ into failed orientation.
summary.what_was_special: The focus's two labels remain co-active: ك ذ ب supplies active counter-attribution, while ض ل ل supplies directional loss, disappearance, or unfindability. Context converts their pairing into navigational, economic, evidentiary, and reception mechanisms without forcing one final reading.
remaining_uncertainties: The focus does not specify whether denial causes straying, straying enables denial, or the two independently define the class.
The provision-denial construction can support conversion, substitution, or a more general description of how provision is treated.
The coating and failed-charge outliers depend on branch-distant material analogies and require explicit qualification.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Active falsification culminates in failed orientation.** `ك ذ ب` **B002** supplies declaring false and `ض ل ل` **B001** going astray from aim. The order reverses 56:51’s `الضالون المكذبون`. **Abductive move:** I infer that reversal permits both arrows to remain visible: straying supports denial, and denial culminates in straying. **Reading change:** the pair is a mutually reinforcing mechanism, not a fixed causal sequence.

2. **Those who declared hidden reality lost.** `ض ل ل` **B002** supplies disappearance and **B003** losing something, while `ك ذ ب` **B001** supplies falsehood against truth. **Abductive move:** I infer that their earlier equation of decomposed invisibility with non-return is now attached to their final classification. **Reading change:** the label preserves the specific epistemic error behind denial.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Hot lodging and fire-contact at 56:93–94 materialized the pair’s two failures as an encompassing reception, not merely labels.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **At final classification, active falsification precedes and explains settled misdirection.** `ك و ن` (B001, being in a state) enters through *min* into `ك ذ ب` (B001, declaring false) followed by `ض ل ل` (B001, deviation from guidance and aim). Ayat 87–91 answer failed reversal with brought-near relief and right-hand peace; ayat 93–96 give this class hot provision, fire-exposure, certainty, and the closing praise command. The packet supplies the same two diagnoses as ayah 51 but reverses their order; I infer a completed feedback loop: earlier deviation supported denial, while repeated denial has now become the cause named before their final lost state. The order sharpens responsibility without erasing error.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 56:93–95 immediately turns the reordered diagnosis into hot provision, fire-exposure, and certified truth, confirming that active falsification now stands first because its consequences have become final.

identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, gerçeğe aykırı söz ve davranışı kapsar; başkasını yalancılıkla niteleme eylemini ya da özel kalıpların bağımsız anlamlarını kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın anlam çekirdeğini verir; kişi betimleyen türevler ile özürlere ilişkin kalıp yalnız kendi sözcüksel karşılıklarında gösterilir ve yalın anlama eklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Bir sözün veya davranışın doğruluğa aykırı olmasıdır. Bu niteliği taşıyan kişi, yalan söyleyen ya da yalanı çokça tekrarlayan biri olarak betimlenebilir.

facets.statement: Doğruluğa aykırılık hem söylenen bir sözde hem de yapılan bir davranışta gerçekleşebilir.
Bu niteliği taşıyan veya onu sıkça gösteren kişi, yalan söyleyen kişi olarak adlandırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, doğruluğa aykırılığı ortak çekirdek sayar; kullanım alanını söz ve davranış olarak verir ve bu niteliği taşıyan kişiye yönelik adlandırmaları aynı anlam çevresinde toplar.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın hem söz hem davranış alanındaki bütün yalın anlam çekirdeğini karşılayan açıklayıcı üst karşılıktır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalnız dişi devenin sütünü konu alan kalıba bağlıdır; genel tükenme veya genel beklenti boşa çıkması anlamına genişletilmez.

root_profile.summary: Kökün anlam ağı, söz ve davranışta doğruluğa aykırılık ile başkasını yalan sayma çekirdeğinden; yükümlülük, savaş hamlesi, gecikmeme, süt kesilmesi, hayvan hareketi, iç benlik ve kumaş görünüşü gibi sözlüksel olarak özelleşmiş alanlara uzanır. Bu alanların bir bölümü yalan veya beklentinin boşa çıkması düşüncesiyle ilişkilendirilebilirken bir bölümü bağımsızlaşmış adlandırmalar olarak kalır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, anlamın çekirdeğini amaçtan, doğru yoldan ve doğruluktan ayrılma olarak kurar; hem yolunu bulamama hem de yanlış ve boş işlere yönelme bu çekirdeğin gerçekleşmeleridir. Başkasını doğru yoldan uzaklaştıran ettirgen kullanım da aynı anlam alanına bağlıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Bu dal fiziksel olarak gözden yitme, bir şeyi kaybetme, unutma ya da kayıp hayvan adı olma anlamlarını içermez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın sapma çekirdeğini korur; yol, arazi, kişiyi sapmış sayma ve bir işi yanlış tutumla yapma gibi kalıba bağlı kullanımları ayrı yüzler olarak sınırlar.

concept_map.definition: Bir kimsenin amaçtan, doğru yoldan veya doğruluktan ayrılması, yolunu bulamaması ya da yanlış ve boş olana yönelmesidir. Ettirgen kullanımda başka biri bu doğrultudan uzaklaştırılır.

facets.statement: Amaçtan, doğru yoldan veya doğruluktan ayrılma ve uygun yönü bulamama anlamın temelidir.
Yanlış, asılsız veya boş işlere yönelme, yönsel sapmanın düşünce ve davranış alanındaki uzantısıdır.
Ettirgen kullanım, başka birini doğru yoldan veya amaçtan uzaklaştırmayı bildirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlatım, doğru yönün ve amacın dışına çıkmayı doğruluk ve kılavuzluk karşıtı bir durum olarak verir; yol bulamama, yoğun sapma, yanlış işlere dalma ve başkasını saptırma bu alan içinde yer alır.

facets.statement: Bir şeyin sahibinden gitmesi ve nerede olduğunun bilinememesi temel yitirme ilişkisidir.

Bir işin elden kaçması ve ona erişecek yolun bulunamaması, yitirme ilişkisinin soyut uzantısıdır.
Öldürülen kişinin kanının öç alınmadan kalması, kaybı karşılıksız kalma sonucuna bağlayan özel kullanımdır.
